```{r}
#| label: setup

source("R/book.R")
```

## QuantLib set-up

Every item uses this process. Time is days over 365 and rates are continuous, so the flat curves reduce to the numeric inputs of RiemannFinMath.

```{r}
#| label: quantlib-process
ql_process <- function(today, spot, rate, dividend, volatility) {
  dc <- QuantLib::Actual365Fixed()
  QuantLib::BlackScholesMertonProcess(
    QuantLib::QuoteHandle(QuantLib::SimpleQuote(spot)),
    QuantLib::YieldTermStructureHandle(QuantLib::FlatForward(ql_date(today), dividend, dc)),
    QuantLib::YieldTermStructureHandle(QuantLib::FlatForward(ql_date(today), rate, dc)),
    QuantLib::BlackVolTermStructureHandle(QuantLib::BlackConstantVol(ql_date(today), QuantLib::NullCalendar(), volatility, dc))
  )
}
ql_type <- function(kind) if (kind == "call") QuantLib::Option_Call_get() else QuantLib::Option_Put_get()
ql_vanilla <- function(kind, strike, exercise) QuantLib::VanillaOption(QuantLib::PlainVanillaPayoff(ql_type(kind), strike), exercise)
```

## Black 76

```{r}
#| label: black-inputs
black <- list(trade = "2023-07-21", maturity = "2023-08-26", forward = 107 + 6.75 / 32, strike = 107.5, volatility = 0.052, rate = 0.05)
black$time <- as.numeric(as.Date(black$maturity) - as.Date(black$trade)) / 365
black$discount <- exp(-black$rate * black$time)
show_inputs(black)
```

```{r}
#| label: black-calls
ql_black <- QuantLib::blackFormula(ql_type("call"), black$strike, black$forward, black$volatility * sqrt(black$time), black$discount)
riemann_black <- RiemannFinMath::forward_option("black", "call", black$forward, black$strike, black$volatility, black$time, black$discount)
calculator <- QuantLib::BlackCalculator(
  QuantLib::PlainVanillaPayoff(ql_type("call"), black$strike), black$forward, black$volatility * sqrt(black$time), black$discount
)
```

```{r}
#| label: black-results
bind_rows(
  compare_values("Value", "price", ql_black, riemann_black$value),
  compare_values("Forward delta", "per unit of forward", calculator$deltaForward(), riemann_black$delta_forward),
  compare_values("Forward gamma", "per unit of forward squared", calculator$gammaForward(), riemann_black$gamma_forward),
  compare_values("Vega", "per unit of volatility", calculator$vega(black$time), riemann_black$vega)
) |>
  show_results()
```

## Bachelier

The legacy text gives the formula and the units in R, without a numeric example on a market. The inputs below are the units of that section: a normal volatility of 40 bp on the 2-year SABR forward.

```{r}
#| label: bachelier
normal <- list(forward = 0.0056, strike = 0.0056, volatility = 0.004, time = 2, discount = 1)
show_inputs(normal)
ql_normal <- map_dbl(c("call", "put"), \(kind) {
  QuantLib::bachelierBlackFormula(ql_type(kind), normal$strike, normal$forward, normal$volatility * sqrt(normal$time), normal$discount)
})
riemann_normal <- RiemannFinMath::forward_option("bachelier", c("call", "put"), normal$forward, normal$strike, normal$volatility, normal$time, normal$discount)
compare_values(c("Call", "Put"), "bp of price", 1e4 * ql_normal, 1e4 * riemann_normal$value) |>
  show_results()
```

## European options and Greeks

```{r}
#| label: european-inputs
equity <- list(today = "2026-01-02", maturity = "2027-01-02", spot = 100, strike = 100, rate = 0.03, dividend = 0, volatility = 0.2)
equity$time <- as.numeric(as.Date(equity$maturity) - as.Date(equity$today)) / 365
show_inputs(equity)
```

QuantLib:

```{r}
#| label: european-quantlib
ql_set_evaluation_date(equity$today)
ql_equity_process <- ql_process(equity$today, equity$spot, equity$rate, equity$dividend, equity$volatility)
ql_call <- ql_vanilla("call", equity$strike, QuantLib::EuropeanExercise(ql_date(equity$maturity)))
QuantLib::Instrument_setPricingEngine(ql_call, QuantLib::AnalyticEuropeanEngine(ql_equity_process))
ql_greeks <- list(
  value = ql_call$NPV(), delta = ql_call$delta(), gamma = ql_call$gamma(), vega = ql_call$vega(), rho = ql_call$rho(),
  dividend_rho = ql_call$dividendRho(), theta = ql_call$theta(), strike_sensitivity = ql_call$strikeSensitivity()
)
```

RiemannFinMath:

```{r}
#| label: european-riemann
riemann_call <- RiemannFinMath::european_option("call", equity$spot, equity$strike, equity$rate, equity$dividend, equity$volatility, equity$time)
```

```{r}
#| label: european-results
units <- c(value = "price", delta = "per unit of spot", gamma = "per unit of spot squared", vega = "per unit of volatility",
           rho = "per unit of rate", dividend_rho = "per unit of yield", theta = "per year", strike_sensitivity = "per unit of strike")
imap(ql_greeks, \(q, name) compare_values(name, units[[name]], q, riemann_call[[name]])) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  show_results()
```

## Implied volatility

```{r}
#| label: implied
ql_implied <- ql_call$impliedVolatility(ql_greeks$value, ql_equity_process, 1e-10, 200L, 1e-7, 4)
riemann_implied <- RiemannFinMath::implied_volatility("call", ql_greeks$value, equity$spot, equity$strike, equity$rate, equity$dividend, equity$time)
compare_values("Implied volatility", "percent", 100 * ql_implied, 100 * riemann_implied) |>
  show_results()
```

## Binomial trees

```{r}
#| label: tree-inputs
tree <- list(today = "2024-03-01", maturity = "2025-03-03", spot = 100, strike = 100, rate = 0.05, dividend = 0, volatility = 0.2)
tree$time <- as.numeric(as.Date(tree$maturity) - as.Date(tree$today)) / 365
show_inputs(tree)
```

```{r}
#| label: tree-calls
ql_set_evaluation_date(tree$today)
ql_tree_process <- ql_process(tree$today, tree$spot, tree$rate, tree$dividend, tree$volatility)
tree_cases <- crossing(exercise = c("european", "american"), steps = c(25L, 100L, 500L))
ql_exercise <- function(kind) {
  if (kind == "american") QuantLib::AmericanExercise(ql_date(tree$today), ql_date(tree$maturity)) else QuantLib::EuropeanExercise(ql_date(tree$maturity))
}
ql_tree <- map2(tree_cases$exercise, tree_cases$steps, \(kind, steps) {
  option <- ql_vanilla("put", tree$strike, ql_exercise(kind))
  QuantLib::Instrument_setPricingEngine(option, QuantLib::BinomialCRRVanillaEngine(ql_tree_process, steps))
  tibble(value = option$NPV(), delta = option$delta(), gamma = option$gamma())
}) |>
  list_rbind()
riemann_tree <- RiemannFinMath::binomial_option(
  "put", tree_cases$exercise, tree$spot, tree$strike, tree$rate, tree$dividend, tree$volatility, tree$time, tree_cases$steps
)
```

```{r}
#| label: tree-results
labels <- paste(tree_cases$exercise, tree_cases$steps, "steps")
bind_rows(
  compare_values(paste(labels, "value"), "price", ql_tree$value, riemann_tree$value),
  compare_values(paste(labels, "delta"), "per unit of spot", ql_tree$delta, riemann_tree$delta),
  compare_values(paste(labels, "gamma"), "per unit of spot squared", ql_tree$gamma, riemann_tree$gamma)
) |>
  show_results()
```

The same European put has an analytic value:

```{r}
#| label: tree-analytic
ql_analytic_put <- ql_vanilla("put", tree$strike, QuantLib::EuropeanExercise(ql_date(tree$maturity)))
QuantLib::Instrument_setPricingEngine(ql_analytic_put, QuantLib::AnalyticEuropeanEngine(ql_tree_process))
compare_values(
  "Analytic European put", "price", ql_analytic_put$NPV(),
  RiemannFinMath::european_option("put", tree$spot, tree$strike, tree$rate, tree$dividend, tree$volatility, tree$time)$value
) |>
  show_results()
```

## Barrier options

The legacy text has no barrier example. The inputs extend the European item above.

```{r}
#| label: barrier
barriers <- tribble(
  ~type,      ~level, ~ql_type,
  "down_in",  80,     list(QuantLib::Barrier_DownIn_get()),
  "down_out", 80,     list(QuantLib::Barrier_DownOut_get()),
  "up_in",    130,    list(QuantLib::Barrier_UpIn_get()),
  "up_out",   130,    list(QuantLib::Barrier_UpOut_get())
)
ql_set_evaluation_date(equity$today)
ql_barrier <- map2_dbl(barriers$ql_type, barriers$level, \(type, level) {
  option <- QuantLib::BarrierOption(
    type[[1]], level, 0, QuantLib::PlainVanillaPayoff(ql_type("call"), equity$strike), QuantLib::EuropeanExercise(ql_date(equity$maturity))
  )
  QuantLib::Instrument_setPricingEngine(option, QuantLib::AnalyticBarrierEngine(ql_equity_process))
  option$NPV()
})
riemann_barrier <- RiemannFinMath::barrier_option(
  "call", barriers$type, equity$spot, equity$strike, barriers$level, 0, equity$rate, equity$dividend, equity$volatility, equity$time
)
compare_values(paste("Call,", barriers$type, barriers$level), "price", ql_barrier, riemann_barrier$value) |>
  show_results()
```

## Monte Carlo

The two sides do not share random numbers, so a Monte Carlo value cannot meet an absolute tolerance of 1e-4 against any other number, and the rows are not judged. The note gives the distance in standard errors.

```{r}
#| label: monte-carlo
mc <- RiemannFinMath::monte_carlo_european(
  "call", equity$spot, equity$strike, equity$rate, equity$dividend, equity$volatility, equity$time,
  paths = 200000, seed = 1234, smoothing = 0.25
)
standard_error <- mc$standard_error
reason <- sprintf(
  "Sampling error: value differs by %.2f standard errors, against the analytic QuantLib value",
  (mc$value - ql_greeks$value) / standard_error
)
bind_rows(
  not_comparable("Value", "price", ql_greeks$value, mc$value, reason),
  not_comparable("Delta", "per unit of spot", ql_greeks$delta, mc$delta, "Sampling error"),
  not_comparable("Gamma, smoothed payoff", "per unit of spot squared", ql_greeks$gamma, mc$gamma, "Sampling error and a smoothed payoff of width 0.25"),
  not_comparable("Vega", "per unit of volatility", ql_greeks$vega, mc$vega, "Sampling error"),
  not_comparable("Theta", "per year", ql_greeks$theta, mc$theta, "Sampling error")
) |>
  show_results()
```

```{r}
#| label: monte-carlo-threads
one_thread <- RiemannFinMath::monte_carlo_european(
  "call", 100, 100, 0.03, 0, 0.2, equity$time, paths = 200000, seed = 1234, threads = 1L
)
four_threads <- RiemannFinMath::monte_carlo_european(
  "call", 100, 100, 0.03, 0, 0.2, equity$time, paths = 200000, seed = 1234, threads = 4L
)
compare_values("Value on 1 and on 4 threads", "price", one_thread$value, four_threads$value, "RiemannFinMath itself") |>
  show_results()
```

## Against LagrangeFinance

The legacy text values the Black 76 option through a process whose spot is the forward and whose dividend yield equals the rate, so the same form is used here. Its implied volatility uses QuantLib's default accuracy of 1e-4 and is not judged, because `implied_volatility` here uses 1e-10.

```{r}
#| label: lagrange
black_as_equity <- RiemannFinMath::european_option("call", black$forward, black$strike, black$rate, black$rate, black$volatility, black$time)
tree_value <- function(kind, steps) riemann_tree$value[tree_cases$exercise == kind & tree_cases$steps == steps]
european_put <- RiemannFinMath::european_option("put", tree$spot, tree$strike, tree$rate, tree$dividend, tree$volatility, tree$time)
bind_rows(
  against_lagrange("Black 76 value", "price", "black.npv", black_as_equity$value),
  against_lagrange("Black 76 delta", "per unit of forward", "black.delta", black_as_equity$delta),
  against_lagrange("Black 76 gamma", "per unit of forward squared", "black.gamma", black_as_equity$gamma),
  against_lagrange("Black 76 vega", "per unit of volatility", "black.vega", black_as_equity$vega),
  against_lagrange("Black 76 theta", "per year", "black.theta", black_as_equity$theta),
  lagrange_not_comparable(
    "Black 76 implied volatility", "percent", "black.implied_volatility_pct",
    100 * RiemannFinMath::implied_volatility("call", black_as_equity$value, black$forward, black$strike, black$rate, black$rate, black$time),
    "Different solver accuracy: 1e-4 against 1e-10"
  ),
  against_lagrange("European put, analytic", "price", "tree.european.analytic", european_put$value),
  against_lagrange("European put, 25 steps", "price", "tree.european.crr_25", tree_value("european", 25L)),
  against_lagrange("European put, 100 steps", "price", "tree.european.crr_100", tree_value("european", 100L)),
  against_lagrange("European put, 500 steps", "price", "tree.european.crr_500", tree_value("european", 500L)),
  against_lagrange("American put, 25 steps", "price", "tree.american.crr_25", tree_value("american", 25L)),
  against_lagrange("American put, 500 steps", "price", "tree.american.crr_500", tree_value("american", 500L)),
  against_lagrange("European call value", "price", "greeks.npv", riemann_call$value),
  against_lagrange("European call delta", "per unit of spot", "greeks.delta", riemann_call$delta),
  against_lagrange("European call gamma", "per unit of spot squared", "greeks.gamma", riemann_call$gamma),
  against_lagrange("European call vega", "per unit of volatility", "greeks.vega", riemann_call$vega),
  against_lagrange("European call theta", "per year", "greeks.theta", riemann_call$theta),
  lagrange_not_comparable(
    "Black 76, Monte Carlo against the formula", "price", "mc.npv", riemann_black$value,
    sprintf("The legacy value is a Monte Carlo estimate with a standard error of %.4f", lagrange_value("mc.standard_error"))
  )
) |>
  show_results()
```

## Not available

Approximation engines (Barone-Adesi-Whaley, Bjerksund-Stensland), Sobol sequences and Longstaff-Schwartz are in the legacy text and not in RiemannFinMath. See @sec-gaps.

## Differences of wrapper and core

```{r}
#| label: design
tribble(
  ~Layer,    ~Aspect,             ~QuantLib,                                                    ~RiemannFinMath,
  "Wrapper", "Set-up",            "Quote, curves, volatility, process, payoff, exercise, engine", "One call with numbers",
  "Wrapper", "Time",              "Evaluation date and maturity date",                          "Time in years",
  "Wrapper", "Many options",      "A loop; one object each",                                    "Vectors recycled to a common length; a table",
  "Wrapper", "Failure",           "An R error from SWIG",                                       "`on_error`: an error, or `NA` with a message per row",
  "Core",    "Greeks",            "Formulas written for each engine",                           "Automatic differentiation of the price",
  "Core",    "Tree delta and gamma", "From the first steps of the tree",                        "The same; other sensitivities are derivatives of the tree",
  "Core",    "Monte Carlo",       "Generators, path objects and statistics classes",            "Pathwise derivatives on path vectors; results depend on the seed and not on the threads"
) |>
  show_design()
```
